comment: Every user-visible string, once, for every shell. The core speaks codes; the shells speak these words. Tools/strings/generate.sh (Core/tools/strings-gen) writes every platform's file from it: Apple's String Catalog and the Swift names, Android's strings.xml, Windows' Resources.resw (040). Keys are dotted lower case; an 'error.<code>' key is the words for a core error code. Arguments are written Apple's way (%@, %d, %1$@; %% for a per cent sign) and every language and platform must take the ones the English takes. A platform's own wording, where it should differ, is an object by language under 'apple', 'android' or 'windows'. British spelling.

address.label.note: Accessibility label of the address field.

address.secure.note: Accessibility label of the padlock shown for an https page.

address.insecure.note: Accessibility label of the warning shown for an http page.

toolbar.open_location.note: Command (Command-L on a Mac): put the keyboard in the address field with the whole address selected.

tabs.list.note: Accessibility label of the strip of the window's tabs.

tabs.untitled.note: The name the strip gives a tab that has no page yet.

tabs.new.note: Button at the end of the strip of tabs, and command (Command-T on a Mac): open an empty tab.

tabs.close.note: Button on a tab in the strip, and command (Command-W on a Mac): close the tab.

menu.history.note: Name of a menu in the Mac's menu bar: going back and forward, and the list of pages visited.

menu.close_window.note: Command in the Mac's File menu (Shift-Command-W): close the window, however many tabs it has.

tabs.next.note: Command in the Mac's Window menu (Control-Tab): bring the next tab in the row in front; from the last, the first.

tabs.previous.note: Command in the Mac's Window menu (Control-Shift-Tab): bring the tab before in the row in front; from the first, the last.

sites.keep.note: Command (Command-D on a Mac, Control-D with a keyboard on Android; in a tab's own menu on a phone): keep the tab as a Site. A Site stays first in the row, and is put to sleep, not closed, when it is closed.

sites.let_go.note: The same command for a tab that is a Site: it becomes a tab like any other again.

sites.site.note: Said of a tab that is kept, to a screen reader, with the tab's name.

sites.asleep.note: Said of a tab that has no page loaded now, to a screen reader, with the tab's name: a Site that was closed, or a tab that came back after a quit. Opening it loads it.

sites.sleep.note: Label of the button at the end of a Site's tab, where another tab has Close Tab: the Site's page is closed and the Site stays in the row.

tabs.reopen.note: Command (Shift-Command-T on a Mac): bring back the tab that was last closed, where it was.

suggestions.list.note: Accessibility label of the list of places offered under the address field as it is typed in.

suggestions.switch_tab.note: At the end of a row of that list which is a tab that is already open: choosing the row brings that tab in front instead of loading the page again.

zoom.open.note: Label of the button, beside the tabs, that opens the zoom bar.

zoom.in.note: Button in the zoom bar, and the command (Command-plus on a Mac): make the page bigger.

zoom.out.note: Button in the zoom bar, and the command (Command-minus on a Mac): make the page smaller.

zoom.reset.note: Accessibility label of the zoom bar's level, which puts the page back to 100% when pressed; and the command (Command-0 on a Mac).

zoom.level.note: The zoom bar's level, in per cent. %ld is the number; %% is a per cent sign.

zoom.done.note: Button that closes the zoom bar.

downloads.title.note: Title of the list of downloads, and the name of its half of the switch beside History.

downloads.empty.en: Files you download will be listed here.
downloads.empty.note: Shown in the Downloads list when nothing has been downloaded.

downloads.clear.note: Button in the Downloads list that takes every download off the list. The files stay where they are.

downloads.done.note: Button that closes the Downloads list.

downloads.stop.note: Accessibility label of the button beside a download that is still coming, which stops it.

downloads.forget.note: Accessibility label of the button beside a download that has ended, which takes it off the list. The file stays.

downloads.older.note: Button at the end of the Downloads list that shows the next, older page of downloads.

downloads.coming.note: Under a download that is still coming, when its size is known: how much has arrived, and how much there is. Both are sizes with their units, such as “1.2 MB”.

downloads.coming_so_far.note: Under a download that is still coming, when its size is not known: how much has arrived, as a size with its unit.

downloads.active.note: Accessibility value of the History and Downloads button while a download is coming.

search.question.title.note: Heading of the first run's question, and of the same list when it is opened again: the person chooses a search engine.

search.question.detail.en: What you type in the address field that is not an address is sent to the search engine you choose. Nothing is sent until you search.
search.question.detail.note: Under the heading of the list of search engines.

search.goes_to.note: On an empty tab, under its hint. %@ is a search engine's own name, such as Ecosia.

search.change.note: Button beside 'Searches go to …' on an empty tab: opens the list of search engines.

search.in_use.note: Said of the search engine that searches go to now, in the list of search engines when it is opened to change it.

search.keep.note: Button that closes the list of search engines without changing where searches go. Not shown at the first run, when one has to be chosen.

search.default.note: Said of the search engine that searches go to when nobody has chosen another, in the list of search engines at the first run.

outside.search.note: Android: the item WebTiger adds to other apps' menu of selected text. Choosing it opens the words as a search in WebTiger, with the search engine the person chose. Short: it sits in a small bar.

search.keep_default.note: Button under the list of search engines at the first run: leaves searches going to the default engine. %@ is that engine's own name, such as DuckDuckGo.

selection.search_with.note: In the menu of words that are selected in a page: search for those words, in a new tab. %@ is the search engine's own name, such as Ecosia.

space.home.note: Name shown for the Space the app made itself, until the person gives it a name. A Space is a set of tabs kept apart from the others, such as home and work.

space.chip.note: Accessibility name of the button at the start of the strip of tabs that says which Space the window shows, and opens the list of Spaces. %@ is the Space's name.

private.new.note: Command in the Mac's File menu (Shift-Command-N): open a private window.

private.chip.note: Chip in the strip of tabs of a private window, where an ordinary window names its Space. Short: on a narrow strip only its first letter is shown.

private.window.note: Name of a private window: the last row of the list of Spaces on a phone (it opens one), the heading of the page that explains it, and what a screen reader says for the chip.

private.row.detail.en: Nothing it visits is kept on this device.
private.row.detail.note: Under 'Private Window' in the list of Spaces.

private.row.open.note: Said beside 'Private Window' in the list of Spaces when a private window is open already: the row then shows it.

private.keeps.en: Nothing you visit in this window is kept on this device: no history, and nothing a site stored once the window is closed. Files you save stay.
private.keeps.note: What a private window means: in an empty tab of one, and on the page behind its chip.

private.hides.en: It does not hide you from the sites you visit, or from your network.
private.hides.note: What a private window does not do: follows the sentence that says what it means.

private.close.note: Button on the page behind a private window's chip, and command: closes the private window, and everything of it is gone.

private.back.note: Button on the page behind a private window's chip on a phone: shows the other window again and leaves the private one open. %@ is the name of the Space the other window shows.

spaces.title.note: Heading of the list of Spaces.

spaces.detail.en: A Space keeps its tabs apart from the others. Choose one to show it in this window.
spaces.detail.note: Under the heading of the list of Spaces.

spaces.shown.note: Said of the Space the window shows now, in the list of Spaces.

spaces.shares.note: Under a Space's name in the list of Spaces, when it is signed in to sites as another Space is. %@ is that other Space's name.

spaces.new.note: Button at the end of the list of Spaces: opens the page that makes one.

spaces.rename.note: Button in the list of Spaces, beside 'New Space…': opens the page that gives the Space the window shows another name or colour.

spaces.done.note: Button that closes the list of Spaces without changing which is shown.

space.new.title.note: Heading of the page that makes a Space.

space.new.name.note: Label of the field for a new Space's name.

space.new.logins.note: Heading over the choice of whose logins a new Space has: its own, or another Space's.

space.new.own.note: Choice for a new Space: it is signed in to nothing, apart from every other Space.

space.new.own.detail.en: Signed out everywhere to begin with. What you sign in to in this Space stays in it.

space.new.shared.note: Choice for a new Space: it is signed in to sites as another Space is.

space.new.shared.detail.en: Signed in wherever %@ is. The two share history and downloads.
space.new.shared.detail.note: Under the choice 'The same as another Space'. %@ is the name of the Space whose logins are shared.

space.new.share_with.note: Label of the choice of which Space a new Space shares its logins with.

space.new.make.note: Button that makes the new Space and shows it in the window.

space.new.back.note: Button on the page that makes a Space: back to the list of Spaces, with nothing made.

space.rename.title.note: Heading of the page that gives a Space another name or colour.

space.rename.save.note: Button that gives the Space the name in the field.

space.colour.note: Heading over the colours to choose among for a Space, where one is made and where one is edited.

space.chosen_colour.note: The same heading when a colour is chosen: it names the colour in words, so that it is not told by the colour alone. %@ is the colour's name, such as Blue.

space.automatic_colour.en: If you choose none, it gets one that no other Space has.
space.automatic_colour.note: Under the colours on the page that makes a Space.

space.no_colour.note: The choice of no colour for a Space, beside the colours.

space.colour.red.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.orange.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.yellow.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.green.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.teal.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.blue.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.purple.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.pink.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

space.colour.grey.note: Name of a colour a Space can have: read by a screen reader for its swatch, and shown beside the heading when it is chosen.

link.menu.note: Accessibility name of the menu shown for a link of a page that was pressed and held.

link.open_new_tab.note: In a link's menu: open the link in a new tab, behind the one being read.

link.open_link_new_tab.note: In the menu a Mac shows for a link (right-click), beside the system's own items such as Copy Link: open the link in a new tab.

link.open_image_new_tab.note: In a picture's menu (on a Mac beside the system's own items such as Copy Image): open the picture by itself in a new tab.

link.download.note: In a link's menu: save what the link leads to as a file, with the person's downloads.

link.image_menu.note: Accessibility name of the menu shown for a picture of a page that was pressed and held.

link.download_image.note: In a picture's menu: save the picture as a file, with the person's downloads.

link.copy.note: In a link's menu: copy the link's address.

link.cancel.note: In a link's menu: close the menu and do nothing.

prompt.permission.note: The sentence in the bar a tab shows when a page asks to use something of the device's. %1$@ is the site, as the address field shows it; %2$@ is what it wants: one or more of the prompt.kind strings, joined as a list by the system (in English: “your camera and your microphone”).

prompt.says.note: The first line of the bar a tab shows when a page says something or asks (alert, confirm, prompt). %@ is the site, as the address field shows it; the page's own words follow on the next lines.

prompt.ok.note: Button in the bar that shows what a page says or asks: accepts it.

prompt.cancel.note: Button in the bar that shows what a page asks: refuses it.

prompt.silence.note: Button in the bar that shows what a page says, from the page's second message on: this page is shown no more messages until another page loads.

prompt.answer.note: Accessibility label of the field in the bar where a page asks for a line of text.

prompt.sign_in.note: The first line of the bar a tab shows when a server asks for a name and a password before it answers (HTTP authentication). %@ is the server, as the address field shows a site: it is who gets what is typed.

prompt.sign_in.again.en: That name or password was not accepted.
prompt.sign_in.again.note: In the sign-in bar, when the server refused what was sent before and asks again.

prompt.sign_in.not_private.en: This connection is not private. What you type could be read by others.
prompt.sign_in.not_private.note: In the sign-in bar, when the server is not reached over https: the name and password travel unprotected.

prompt.sign_in.name.note: The sign-in bar's first field: the name to sign in with. Shown in the empty field and read as its label.

prompt.sign_in.password.note: The sign-in bar's second field. Shown in the empty field and read as its label.

prompt.sign_in.go.note: Button in the sign-in bar: sends the name and the password to the server that asked.

prompt.download.note: The sentence in the bar a tab shows when a page starts a download and its site was not yet allowed to. %1$@ is the site, as the address field shows it; %2$@ is the name the file would be saved under, in quotation marks so that where it begins and ends can be seen.

prompt.kind.camera.note: What a page asks to use, in the prompt.permission sentence.

prompt.kind.microphone.note: What a page asks to use, in the prompt.permission sentence.

prompt.kind.location.note: What a page asks to use, in the prompt.permission sentence: where the device is.

prompt.allow.note: Button in a tab's prompt: lets the site use what it asked for, now and when it asks again.

prompt.refuse.note: Button in a tab's prompt: refuses what the page asked for, this time.

permissions.title.note: Title of the list of sites that were allowed to download, or to use the camera, the microphone or the location, and the name of its part of the switch beside History and Downloads.

permissions.empty.en: Sites you allow to download, or to use your camera, microphone or location, will be listed here.
permissions.empty.note: Shown in the Permissions list when no site was allowed anything.

permissions.clear.note: Button in the Permissions list that takes back what every site was allowed. Each will ask again.

permissions.done.note: Button that closes the Permissions list.

permissions.forget.note: Accessibility label of the button beside a site in the Permissions list, which takes back what it was allowed. The site will ask again.

permissions.kind.camera.note: What a site was allowed to use, under its name in the Permissions list. Several are joined as a list by the system.

permissions.kind.microphone.note: What a site was allowed to use, under its name in the Permissions list.

permissions.kind.location.note: What a site was allowed to use, under its name in the Permissions list: where the device is.

permissions.kind.downloads.note: What a site was allowed to do, under its name in the Permissions list: download files without asking each time.

find.open.note: Label of the button, beside the tabs, that opens the find bar; and the command (Command-F on a Mac).

find.field.note: Placeholder and accessibility label of the find bar's field.

find.previous.note: Button in the find bar: go to the match before.

find.next.note: Button in the find bar: go to the next match.

find.done.note: Button that closes the find bar.

find.none.note: Shown in the find bar when the text is not on the page.

find.count.note: Shown in the find bar where the engine counts: which match is shown, and how many there are. First %ld is the match's number, second the total.

history.open.note: Label of the button, beside the tabs, that opens the lists of pages visited and of files downloaded.

history.title.note: Title of the list of pages visited.

history.done.note: Button that closes the History list.

history.search.note: Placeholder and accessibility label of the field for finding a visit by words of its title or address.

history.empty.en: Pages you visit will be listed here.
history.empty.note: Shown in the History list when nothing has been visited yet.

history.none_found.note: Shown in the History list when the words typed find no visit.

history.forget.note: Accessibility label of the button beside a visit that removes it from history.

history.older.note: Button at the end of the History list that shows the next, older page of visits.

history.clear.note: Button in the History list that asks which visits to forget.

history.clear.title.note: Question asked by the Clear button of the History list, above the choices.

history.clear.detail.en: Visits that are forgotten can’t be brought back.
history.clear.detail.note: Under the question of which visits to forget.

history.clear.hour.note: Choice: forget the visits of the last hour.

history.clear.today.note: Choice: forget the visits since midnight.

history.clear.cancel.note: Choice: leave history as it is.

tab.empty.title.note: Heading of a tab that has no page yet.

tab.empty.hint.en: Type an address or a search above.
tab.empty.hint.note: Hint under the heading of an empty tab.

error.title.note: Heading shown over a page that failed to load.

error.retry.note: Button on the failed-page view: reload.

certificate.advanced.note: Button on the page shown when a site's certificate isn't trusted, under 'Try Again': shows the warning, and under it the way to go on to the site all the same.

certificate.warning.title.note: Heading of the warning shown before a person can go on to a site whose certificate isn't trusted.

certificate.warning.en: WebTiger can’t confirm that this is really %@. Someone could be pretending to be it, and could read or change what you send and receive: passwords, messages, card numbers.
certificate.warning.note: The warning shown before a person can go on to a site whose certificate isn't trusted. %@ is the site's host name, such as router.example.com.

certificate.warning.only_if.en: Go on only if you know why this site’s certificate isn’t trusted, such as a router or a device of your own.
certificate.warning.only_if.note: Second sentence of the warning before going on to a site whose certificate isn't trusted.

certificate.proceed.note: Button under the warning: loads the site although its certificate isn't trusted. %@ is the site's host name. The words in brackets say what the button does and must stay.

error.net.offline.en: You’re not connected to the internet.

error.net.dns.en: The site’s address couldn’t be found.

error.net.connect.note: A load failed: connection refused or lost.

error.net.timeout.en: The site took too long to answer.

error.net.tls.en: A secure connection to the site couldn’t be made.
error.net.tls.note: A load failed: TLS or certificate problem.

error.net.tls.untrusted.en: This device doesn’t trust this site’s certificate.
error.net.tls.untrusted.note: A load failed: the site's certificate signs itself, or was signed by an authority this device does not know.

error.net.tls.date.en: This site’s certificate isn’t valid today. It may have run out, or this device’s date may be wrong.
error.net.tls.date.note: A load failed: the site's certificate has expired or is not valid yet, by this device's clock.

error.net.tls.name.en: This site’s certificate is for a different site.
error.net.tls.name.note: A load failed: the certificate the site presented names another site.

error.net.failed.en: Something went wrong while loading the page.
error.net.failed.note: A load failed for a reason without words of its own.

error.page.renderer_gone.note: The process drawing the page died.

error.download.cancelled.note: Under a download that was stopped.

error.download.network.note: Under a download that failed because of the network.

error.download.disk.note: Under a download that failed because its file could not be written.

error.download.interrupted.en: WebTiger was closed before it finished.
error.download.interrupted.note: Under a download that was still coming when the app ended.

error.download.failed.note: Under a download that failed for a reason this build has no words for.

error.download.missing.en: The file isn’t where it was saved any more.
error.download.missing.note: Under a download in the list, after a person pressed it to open its file: the file was moved, renamed or removed since it was downloaded.

error.system.no_handler.en: Nothing on this device opens this kind of file.
error.system.no_handler.note: Under a download in the list, after a person pressed it to open its file: no app on the device opens files of its kind.

downloads.open_failed.note: Under a download in the list, after a person pressed it to open its file, when it did not open for a reason this build has no words for.

downloads.open.note: What pressing a finished download in the list does, as a screen reader says it: opens the file with whatever the device has for its kind.

error.engine.no_profiles.en: The web engine on this device can’t keep each Space’s logins separate. Update Android System WebView and try again.
error.engine.no_profiles.note: Android: the System WebView is too old to give each login set a profile of its own.

error.engine.no_private.en: Private windows aren’t available on this device yet.
error.engine.no_private.note: The engine cannot make a login set that is kept in memory only.

error.engine.unavailable.note: The web engine the tab asked for is not installed.

error.space.too_many.en: There are as many Spaces as there can be.
error.space.too_many.note: Said on the page that makes a Space when the app will not make another: it has its limit of them.

error.space.name_empty.note: Said on the page that makes a Space when the name is empty.

error.space.unknown.en: That Space isn’t there any more.
error.space.unknown.note: Said on the page that makes a Space when the Space whose logins it was to share is gone.

error.space.failed.note: Said on the page that makes a Space when it could not be made and no more is known.

error.space.rename_failed.note: Said on the page that edits a Space when it could not be changed and no more is known.

error.space.colour_unknown.en: That colour isn’t one a Space can have.
error.space.colour_unknown.note: Said where a Space is made or edited when the app does not know the colour that was chosen.

catalogue.title.note: Title of the design catalogue: a screen for designers that shows every design token and every state of the window.

catalogue.colours.note: Design catalogue: heading of the colour tokens.

catalogue.space.note: Design catalogue: heading of the spacing tokens.

catalogue.radius.note: Design catalogue: heading of the corner-radius tokens.

catalogue.size.note: Design catalogue: heading of the size tokens.

catalogue.states.note: Design catalogue: heading of the browser window's states.

catalogue.state.loading.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.secure.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.suggestions.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.zoom.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.downloads_list.note: Design catalogue: a state of the Downloads list.

catalogue.state.downloads_empty.note: Design catalogue: a state of the Downloads list.

catalogue.state.prompt_alert.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.prompt_confirm.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.prompt_text.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.search_question.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.

catalogue.state.link_menu.note: Design catalogue: a state of the window.
